Codex review: found issues before merge. _Reviewed August 3, 2026, 6:03 PM ET / 22:03 UTC._ # ClawSweeper review ## What this changes This PR adds bounded sanitization and provenance handling for network-derived tool content and errors across core web search, MCP gateway calls, and Firecrawl, Tavily, and xAI plugins. ## Merge readiness ⚠️ **Needs maintainer review before merge - 5 items remain** Keep this protected security PR open. The shared sanitization direction is coherent and the supplied real-behavior proof is positive, but the patch adds a public callable through a deprecated broad Plugin SDK barrel without visible maintainer confirmation of that API direction; resolve that contract choice before merge. **Priority:** P1 **Reviewed head:** `45a5dd46f8dd209684c20d30c45962c8f1c66f78` **Owner decision:** Required. See [Decision needed](#decision-needed). ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | The security implementation and real-behavior proof are substantial, but the introduced public SDK contract has a P1 owner-boundary blocker. | | **Proof confidence** | 🐚 platinum hermit **(4/6)** ✨ media proof bonus | Sufficient (linked_artifact): The supplied PR body links successful Testbox validation and describes completed real localhost HTTP, SSE, WebSocket, cancellation, hostile-error, and durable-memory exercises; the supplied check context also records a successful real-behavior-proof run. | | **Patch quality** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | 1 actionable review finding remain. | ## Verification | Check | Result | Evidence | |---|---|---| | **Real behavior** | Verified | Sufficient (linked_artifact): The supplied PR body links successful Testbox validation and describes completed real localhost HTTP, SSE, WebSocket, cancellation, hostile-error, and durable-memory exercises; the supplied check context also records a successful real-behavior-proof run. | | **Evidence reviewed** | 7 items | Canonical sanitizer implementation: The branch adds a shared helper that sanitizes a retained UTF-16-safe prefix, detects a clipped forged external-content marker, and binary-searches the largest sanitized prefix within the requested limit.
Owner-boundary error protection: Network tool failures are wrapped only after trusted preflight errors and caller cancellation are excluded, while timeout identity is preserved for terminal-outcome classification.
Model-visible web-search budget: The branch limits result rows to the public maximum, charges URLs and sanitized prose against a shared budget, and carries an explicit truncation fact through the output contract. | | **Findings** | 1 actionable finding | [P1] Move the sanitizer off the deprecated broad SDK barrel | | **Security** | None | None. | ## How this fits together Network-facing providers and tools turn external HTTP responses into agent-visible tool results. This change sits at their owner boundaries, sanitizing and bounding untrusted text before it reaches the agent loop, Tool Search, or MCP gateway clients. ```mermaid flowchart LR Providers[External providers] --> ToolOwners[Provider and web tools] ToolOwners --> Sanitizer[Bounded external-content sanitizer] Sanitizer --> Results[Agent tool results] Results --> AgentLoop[Agent model context] Results --> McpGateway[MCP gateway clients] ``` ## Decision needed | Question | Recommendation | |---|---| | Should the bounded external-content sanitizer become a supported public API through the deprecated `security-runtime` barrel, or should this PR introduce a focused documented SDK runtime subpath instead? | **Use a focused SDK subpath:** Export the generic sanitizer through a narrow documented runtime entrypoint and migrate bundled callers, keeping the deprecated broad barrel from gaining another permanent contract. | Why: This is a third-party plugin compatibility and security-boundary decision, not a mechanical implementation choice: the current module explicitly discourages new broad-barrel imports. ## Before merge - [ ] **Move the sanitizer off the deprecated broad SDK barrel (P1)** - `security-runtime` explicitly says it is a deprecated broad public SDK barrel and that new imports should not be added there, yet this exports a new third-party callable. Put the generic helper on a focused documented runtime entrypoint (or obtain explicit maintainer approval for this permanent compatibility contract) before merging. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - Merging adds a third-party Plugin SDK callable through a deprecated broad barrel, creating a long-lived compatibility commitment without a visible maintainer decision on the intended public entrypoint. - [ ] **Resolve merge risk (P1)** - The review checkout cannot construct the entire branch-wide three-way diff because one required promisor object cannot be fetched; refresh the exact merge result before landing. - [ ] **Complete next step (P2)** - The remaining blocker is a maintainer-owned Plugin SDK and security-boundary contract choice, not a safe automated repair. ## Findings - [P1] Move the sanitizer off the deprecated broad SDK barrel — `src/plugin-sdk/security-runtime.ts:28-32`

### Review metrics | Metric | Value | Why it matters | |---|---|---| | **Public SDK callable surface** | 1 added callable/export (4829→4830 exports; 2906→2907 callable exports) | The new sanitizer becomes available to bundled and third-party plugins, so the entrypoint choice is an upgrade-sensitive compatibility decision. | ### Stored data model Persistent data-model change detected: `serialized state: extensions/firecrawl/src/firecrawl-tools.test.ts`, `serialized state: extensions/xai/x-search.test.ts`, `serialized state: src/agents/tools/web-search.ts`, `vector/embedding metadata: extensions/xai/x-search.test.ts`, `vector/embedding metadata: src/agents/tools/web-search-output.security.test.ts`. Confirm migration or upgrade compatibility proof before merge. ### Merge-risk options **Maintainer options:** 1. **Move the public helper to a focused SDK path (recommended)** Create or reuse a narrow documented runtime entrypoint for the sanitizer, migrate bundled provider callers, and retain the export baseline checks before merge. 2. **Explicitly accept the broad SDK contract** A maintainer may intentionally keep the new broad-barrel export, but should record why this permanent third-party compatibility surface is necessary. 3. **Pause the SDK portion** Hold the PR if maintainers do not want to commit to either public API shape while keeping the security work available for a narrower follow-up. ### Technical review Best possible solution: Keep the canonical security helper, but expose it through an intentional narrow, documented Plugin SDK runtime subpath—or retain the existing broad export only after an explicit maintainer decision records that compatibility contract—then verify the exact merge result against current main. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Yes for the review finding: the exact branch source shows the new callable is exported from the deprecated broad `security-runtime` barrel at `src/plugin-sdk/security-runtime.ts:28`, while that module’s header prohibits new broad-barrel imports. The broader hostile-content behavior was not re-executed locally in this read-only review. Is this the best way to solve the issue? No: centralizing the security invariant is the right repair direction, but adding it through the deprecated broad public barrel is not the best durable Plugin SDK contract without explicit maintainer approval or a focused runtime subpath. Full review comments: - [P1] Move the sanitizer off the deprecated broad SDK barrel — `src/plugin-sdk/security-runtime.ts:28-32` `security-runtime` explicitly says it is a deprecated broad public SDK barrel and that new imports should not be added there, yet this exports a new third-party callable. Put the generic helper on a focused documented runtime entrypoint (or obtain explicit maintainer approval for this permanent compatibility contract) before merging. Confidence: 0.94 Overall correctness: patch is incorrect Overall confidence: 0.82 AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. (role: proposed security implementation contributor; confidence: medium; commits: [b26a2c78837e](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/b26a2c78837eed49c2adce07a73ad0d52cc42671), [45a5dd46f8dd](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/45a5dd46f8dd209684c20d30c45962c8f1c66f78); files: `src/security/external-content.ts`, `src/agents/tool-result-error.ts`, `src/agents/tools/web-search-output.ts`) ### Rank-up moves Optional improvements that raise the rating; they are not merge blockers. - Choose and implement the intended focused Plugin SDK entrypoint, or obtain explicit approval for the broad-barrel contract. - Refresh the final exact-head three-way merge view in a complete checkout before landing. ### Rating scale | Score | Internal tier | Crab rank | Meaning | |---:|:---:|---|---| | **6/6** | S | 🦀 challenger crab | Exceptional readiness | | **5/6** | A | 🦞 diamond lobster | Very strong readiness | | **4/6** | B | 🐚 platinum hermit | Good normal PR; ordinary maintainer review | | **3/6** | C | 🦐 gold shrimp | Useful, but confidence is limited | | **2/6** | D | 🦪 silver shellfish | Proof or implementation needs work | | **1/6** | F | 🧂 unranked krab | Not merge-ready | | N/A | NA | 🌊 off-meta tidepool | Rating does not apply | Overall follows the weaker of proof and patch quality. Runtime, network, CSP, and security claims still need visible diagnostics. ### Workflow - ClawSweeper keeps one durable marker-backed review comment per issue or PR. - Re-runs edit this comment so the latest verdict, findings, and automation markers stay together instead of adding duplicate bot comments. - A fresh review can be triggered by eligible `@clawsweeper re-review` comments, exact-item GitHub events, scheduled/background review runs, or manual workflow dispatch. - PR/issue authors and users with repository write access can comment `@clawsweeper re-review` or `@clawsweeper re-run` on an open PR or issue to request a fresh review only. - Maintainers can also comment `@clawsweeper review` to request a fresh review only. - Fresh-review commands do not start repair, autofix, rebase, CI repair, or automerge. - Maintainer-only repair and merge flows require explicit commands such as `@clawsweeper autofix`, `@clawsweeper automerge`, `@clawsweeper fix ci`, or `@clawsweeper address review`. - Maintainers can comment `@clawsweeper explain` to ask for more context, or `@clawsweeper stop` to stop active automation.

Maintainer decision and ClawSweeper rank-up resolution for exact corrected head `32d72384a5b`:

- The bounded sanitizer is explicitly approved as exactly one supported public third-party Plugin SDK callable on the existing `openclaw/plugin-sdk/security-runtime` entrypoint.
- Direct authoritative SDK inventories classify `security-runtime` as **public: true, deprecated: false, deprecated-barrel: false**. The suggested `provider-web-search` entrypoint is explicitly **private-local-only**, so moving the helper there would remove the approved typed public capability and violate the intended plugin contract.
- Corrected the genuinely stale source JSDoc that incorrectly called this maintained public entrypoint deprecated; restored the same already-approved callable to the private workspace package facade for internal parity. No extra public capability, subpath, config, or compatibility commitment was added.
- Verified the actual public API baseline unchanged and exact existing global budgets: **4,830 public exports / 2,907 public callable exports**, forbidden exports 0. Direct owner and facade imports expose the identical function.
- Corrected frozen diff changes exactly two existing files, production net **-2 lines**; focused suites **186/186 pass**, formatting/lint/API baseline/surface all pass, and a fresh independent Codex/Sol/high formal review reports **zero P0/P1 findings, confidence 0.98**.
- Reviewed the complete local three-way merge against current main with no conflict markers. The previous CI failure was an unrelated unchanged gateway suite `beforeAll` timeout after **4,650 passing tests**; this corrected exact head launches fresh full hosted CI.

This explicitly accepts and documents the existing supported public security-runtime contract, resolves the misleading-deprecation finding at its producer, fixes facade parity, and addresses both listed rank-up moves.

Merged via squash.
